events.text: The inner-disciple examination is announced. Pass, and you get a better manual, a better room and a master who actually remembers your name.

ok.log: You pass. Your new room has a window. Your new manual has fewer mistakes in it. Life is good.

fail.log: You fail by one question. The examiner writes 'next year' on your paper, which is the kindest thing an examiner has ever done.

effects.log: You study all year. Next time, you will be ready.

events.text: The sect leader summons you. 'Your progress has been noticed. We would like to name you a core disciple of {sect}.'

effects.log: Your name is written on the wall of the main hall. Juniors bow when you pass. It takes a month to stop looking behind you to see who they are bowing to.

choices.text: Ask to stay a simple disciple

effects.log: The leader studies you for a long time. 'Humility, or cunning?' the leader asks. You do not answer. The leader smiles.

events.text: An elder's seat on the council of {sect} is empty. Every eye in the sect turns to you.

effects.log: You sit on the council. You discover that being an elder is mostly meetings. Long ones.

choices.text: Recommend someone else and keep training

effects.log: Someone else gets the meetings. You get the mountain to yourself.

events.text: You find the sect library empty at midnight, and one cabinet has been left unlocked.

ok.log: An elder's personal notes on the manual you are learning. Half of your mistakes, explained in a page.

fail.log: The library guardian was not asleep. Your punishment involves a very long staircase.

choices.text: Lock it and tell the librarian

effects.log: The librarian gives you a look you cannot read. Next week, a useful scroll appears on your desk.

events.text: Monthly pill allocation. There is one Marrow Pill left, and two disciples in line: you, and a nervous junior who is about to fail a breakthrough without it.

effects.log: The junior says nothing. You hear, later, that the breakthrough failed.
The junior breaks through and tells the whole sect who gave up the pill. People start calling you 'senior brother' and 'senior sister' like they mean it.

events.text: {npc}, a senior disciple, has decided that you will do {his} chores, wash {his} robes and call {him} 'great senior'.

mem.note: humiliated me in the training yard

ok.log: You win in front of the whole yard. You do your own chores. So, from now on, does {npc}.

fail.log: {npc} wins, barely, and seems rattled that it was so close. The chores stop anyway.

effects.log: You wash the robes and watch {him} train. You learn all of {his} weaknesses. Every single one.

events.text: A senior disciple, {npc}, finds you practising alone after dark. 'My own master never bothered with me either,' {he} says, and takes off {his} outer robe. 'Again. Slower.'

mem.note: let me teach them at night

effects.log: For a year {npc} corrects you every night. You become good. More than that, you become friends.
{npc} shrugs. 'Suit yourself.' You regret it for years.

events.text: A jade token has gone missing from the treasury, and the only footprints outside are the same size as yours.

choices.text: Investigate and find the real thief

ok.log: The real thief is the treasurer's nephew, who has very small feet and very large debts. The treasurer apologises to you in public. It is glorious.

fail.log: You cannot prove it. You serve thirty days in the punishment cave. The token turns up a month later in the nephew's room.

choices.text: Ask your master to vouch for you

effects.log: Your master stands up in the hall and says one sentence: 'My disciple does not steal.' The matter ends there.

events.text: The founding festival of {sect}. Lanterns on every roof, disciples performing forms for the villagers, too much food.

choices.text: Perform a sword form for the crowd

ok.log: The children in the crowd go silent, then roar. Somewhere in the back, a small child picks up a stick and starts copying you.

fail.log: You drop your sword in front of three hundred people. The applause is very polite.

effects.log: You chop mountains of vegetables and eat the best dumplings of your life.

events.text: Two villages are about to go to war over a well. The sect sends you to settle it.

ok.log: You get them to dig a second well together. Your name gets carved on it, spelled wrong. You love it.

fail.log: Both villages end up angry at you instead of each other. Technically, the war is averted.

choices.text: Settle it with a show of force

effects.log: You split a boulder with your palm in the square. Everybody stops arguing. Nobody is happy, but everybody is polite.

events.text: A Demonic Cult practitioner has been draining the qi of travellers on the southern road. The sect sends you to hunt them.

ok.log: You find them in an old shrine. It is a hard fight. You bring back a black lotus badge as proof.

fail.deathCause: a Demonic Cult practitioner on the southern road
fail.log: They were stronger than the sect said. You escape with your life and a lesson about sect intelligence.

choices.text: Set a trap with the local militia

ok.log: Nets, torches, twenty farmers with pitchforks and one very surprised practitioner.

fail.log: The practitioner sees through the trap and escapes. Two farmers are hurt. You carry that home.

events.text: The family council is divided: the elders want to marry the young head's sister to a rival family for an alliance. She does not want to.

effects.log: The alliance is made. The family grows stronger. The sister does not look at you at the wedding.

ok.log: You convince them to seal the alliance with trade instead. The sister sends you a letter of thanks, and a very good tea.

fail.log: The elders are annoyed. The wedding goes ahead anyway. You tried.

events.text: The family head is old, and the succession contest has begun. Your name is on the list, and so is your cousin's, who has been preparing for this since birth.

ok.log: You win. The cousin congratulates you with a face like carved stone. You are the heir to {sect}.

fail.log: Your cousin wins. You bow first, in front of everyone. It earns you more respect than winning would have.

effects.log: Your cousin becomes heir. From that day on, they owe you, and everyone knows it.

events.text: A rival stronghold has moved into your river port. The boss wants them gone by the full moon.

ok.log: By the full moon the port is yours again. The boss gives you a gold-hilted knife and a look of new respect.

fail.log: The raid goes badly. You are pulled from the river by your own people.

ok.log: Half the port, no blood. The boss grumbles, then quietly admits it was the smarter move.

fail.log: They laugh at the offer. The boss laughs at you. Nobody laughs for long.

events.text: The stronghold is smuggling salt past the government checkpoint, and you are in charge of the boats tonight.

effects.log: Forty taels out, a hundred in. The guards wave and wish you a pleasant evening.

ok.log: Three boats, no lights, total silence. The fog loves you tonight.

fail.log: A lantern swings toward you. You dump the salt in the river and swim for it.

events.text: The boss orders you to burn a village that refused to pay. You look at the children in the doorways.

effects.log: You do it. At night, for years, you smell smoke that is not there.

choices.text: Warn them first and burn empty houses

ok.log: Nobody dies. The boss never finds out. The villagers rebuild, and one of them leaves rice cakes at the crossroads for you, every year.

fail.log: The boss finds out. You survive the punishment. Barely.

effects.log: You ride out alone. You are a wanderer now, with enemies behind you and a clean conscience ahead.

events.text: The Cult tests the loyalty of every new member. Yours: stand guard all night over a prisoner who begs you, calmly, to let him go.

effects.log: You do not move all night. At dawn the elder nods. You have passed. You do not sleep well for a week.

ok.log: He vanishes into the dark. Nobody ever finds out. Years later, a stranger saves your life and says only: 'The prisoner remembers.'

fail.log: It was the test. The prisoner was an elder. The punishment is long, and you survive it.

events.text: You are summoned before the Heavenly Demon. The hall is so quiet you can hear the torches breathe.

effects.log: He places a hand on your head. Knowledge pours into you like cold water. 'Do not disappoint me,' he says.

ok.log: The hall freezes. Then he laughs. 'Finally, someone with a spine.' You leave with his favour and a hundred new enemies.

fail.log: He does not laugh. You are carried out.

events.text: A purge sweeps the Cult. Someone has been passing secrets to the Orthodox Alliance, and suspicion falls on everyone.

ok.log: The purge passes over you like a storm cloud. Three of your neighbours are gone by the end of the month.

fail.log: You are questioned for three days. They let you go. You will never feel safe here again.

ok.log: You find them first. The Cult rewards you. You try not to think about what happens to the traitor.

fail.log: You accuse the wrong person. The real traitor thanks you with a smile you will never forget.

events.text: You have stayed too long. Your hands have done things your heart did not agree with. There is a gap in the patrol at the third watch.

ok.log: You walk out under the stars. By dawn you are three mountains away. The Cult will remember. So will you.

fail.log: They catch you at the river. You fight free, badly hurt, and keep running.

choices.text: Stay, and do what good you can from inside

effects.log: You quietly warn villages before raids and lose prisoners' paperwork. It is not much. It is something.

events.text: The sect asks you to teach the newest class of disciples for a season. They are twelve years old and terrible.

effects.log: Teaching the basics makes you see them fresh. One of the children has real talent. You start watching them closely.

choices.text: Make them run laps and meditate

effects.log: They run, you meditate. Everybody gets stronger, in a way.

events.text: A child named {npc} has been waiting outside your door since dawn. '{His} parents died last winter,' the gatekeeper says. 'The child says {he} will only learn from you.'

mem.note: took me in as a disciple

effects.log: {npc} bows nine times. From that day on, there is someone who calls you 'master'.
{npc} goes to the outer hall. {He} does not look back. You wonder about {him} for years.

events.text: Your disciple {npc} is stuck at the gate of the next realm and asks you to guard {his} breakthrough.

effects.log: You guide {his} energy through the gate. {npc} breaks through with tears in {his} eyes. You feel prouder than of your own.

mem.note: trusted me to do it alone

ok.log: {npc} breaks through alone and walks out of the cave a different person.

mem.note: left me alone when I needed them

fail.log: {npc} fails, and does not speak to you for a month.

events.text: The sect's seclusion cave is free for a season. It is cold, dark and perfectly silent.

effects.log: Three months alone with your breath. You come out paler and stronger, and talk too loudly for a week.

choices.text: Give your slot to a friend

effects.log: Your friend comes out stronger and grateful. You come out of nothing, but you have a friend for life.

events.text: The leader of {sect} is dying. At the bedside, with shaking hands, the leader offers you a sealed scroll. 'Do not open it until the sect needs it.'

effects.log: You keep it under your pillow. The sect has no idea it exists. Yet.

choices.text: Ask that it go to the heir

effects.log: A tired smile. 'That is why I wanted you to have it.' The scroll goes to the heir anyway.

events.text: The sect is split in two, one faction ready to join the Demonic Cult for protection. You remember the scroll under your pillow.

choices.text: Open it before the whole sect

effects.log: It names you guardian of the sect until a new leader is chosen, and holds the leader's final technique. The traitor faction kneels. You did not expect the manual. Neither did anyone else.
The final technique of the leader. You keep it quiet. The sect splits anyway. You wonder if you chose wrong.

events.text: Word of your deeds has reached the council. They summon you to the main hall, and they are not smiling.

ok.log: You talk your way through it, barely. You are on probation. Everyone watches you now.

fail.log: Expelled. Your name is struck from the rolls in front of everyone. You walk down the thousand steps alone.

choices.text: Leave before they can expel you

effects.log: You leave your jade token on the altar and walk out. No one stops you.

events.text: At midnight, the sect gates open from the inside. A traitor has let the Demonic Cult in.

ok.log: You hold the hall until dawn. When the sun rises, the Cult retreats and the sect sings your name.

fail.deathCause: the night the sect gates opened
fail.log: You fall at the doors of the hall, and are found alive under three enemies.

choices.text: Get the juniors out through the back

ok.log: Forty children, one secret path, no losses. Years later, every one of them will say your name first.

fail.log: You save most of them. Most.

events.text: The sect's cat has chosen you. It sleeps on your manuals, eats your dinner and sits on your face during meditation.

effects.log: Disciples start calling you 'the Cat Elder'. Your meditation actually improves. You suspect the cat is a hidden master.
The cat returns by nightfall and sits on your face with renewed determination.

events.text: After a year of practising 'Palm of Ten Thousand Mountains', you learn it was a copying mistake. It was meant to be 'Palm of Ten Thousand Mountain Goats'.

effects.log: Your mistaken version turns out to be better. The library quietly updates the manual.
The goat version is mostly about balance. It is, annoyingly, very useful.

events.text: You find the strictest elder in the sect asleep under a tree, snoring, with a half-eaten persimmon in one hand.

effects.log: He never mentions it. But for the next year, he is strangely kind to you in the training yard.
The sect laughs for a week. The elder assigns you to latrine duty for a month. He knows.

events.text: You reach the final of the inter-sect tournament. Your opponent, {npc}, bows politely and then looks at you like a hungry wolf.

mem.note: beat me in the tournament final

ok.log: You win the final. The crowd chants your name. {npc} bows again, stiffly, and walks off to train.

mem.note: gave me the best fight of my life

fail.log: You lose, but it is the fight people talk about for years. {npc} offers you a hand up.

choices.text: Fight to learn, not to win

mem.note: fought me with an open heart

effects.log: You lose on points and learn more in one fight than in a year. {npc} buys you dinner afterwards.

events.text: A group of disciples sneaks out to the town below for a night of noodles and lanterns. They invite you.

ok.log: The best noodles of your life and a friendship with three people who will matter later.

fail.log: Caught climbing back over the wall. The punishment is worth it, you decide, chewing the last noodle.

effects.log: You train in the empty yard under the moon. You can hear them laughing all the way from town.

events.text: In a teahouse, disciples from a rival sect mock {sect} loudly enough for everyone to hear.

ok.log: They leave the teahouse with less honour than they came in with. The owner sends a free pot of tea to your table.

fail.log: They leave laughing. You leave limping. You will remember their faces.

choices.text: Pay for their tea and leave

effects.log: They stop laughing, confused. One of them bows slightly as you leave.

events.text: The Bandit King of Black Ox Mountain has taken a magistrate's daughter hostage. The sect sends you, and only you.

ok.log: You fight your way to the top and bring her down the mountain on your back. The magistrate weeps. The Bandit King does not.

fail.deathCause: the Bandit King of Black Ox Mountain
fail.log: The Bandit King is no rumour. You barely escape down the mountain.

choices.text: Go in disguised as a bandit

ok.log: Three days as a bandit. You are, frankly, very good at it. On the fourth night you walk out with the hostage and the king's treasure map.

fail.log: Your disguise lasts one dinner. You escape through the latrine. It is not heroic.

events.text: The sect treasury is empty after a bad year, and the elders ask disciples to contribute what they can.

effects.log: Your name goes on the benefactors' tablet. Juniors whisper it. You pretend not to hear.
A winter of hunting. The sect survives. So do you, with scars on your forearms.
Some disciples notice. Most do not. You notice.

events.text: As an elder, you must vote: merge {sect} with a stronger neighbour for safety, or stay independent and risk everything.

effects.log: The sect survives, under a new name. The old disciples never quite forgive you.

ok.log: The sect stays itself, and against all odds, it thrives. You are remembered as the elder who believed.

fail.log: Three lean years. The sect survives, barely, and some blame you.

events.text: The family has arranged a match for you with {npc} of an allied family. You meet for the first time at a formal tea. {He} looks as trapped as you feel.

mem.note: married me for the family, and was kind anyway

effects.log: You marry in autumn. It is not love. Not at first. By the second winter you are not sure any more.

mem.note: was honest with me when no one else was

effects.log: You both admit you do not want this. Together, you convince both families to call it off. You end up close friends.

events.text: The Orthodox Alliance holds its great assembly, and {sect} sends you as its representative. The great sects look down their noses at everyone.

choices.text: Speak boldly for the smaller sects

ok.log: Your speech makes the old masters shift in their seats. Small sects start sending you letters and gifts.

fail.log: The great sects smile politely and ignore you completely.

effects.log: You leave with three new allies and a very good idea of who really runs the Alliance.
